The Rufous-tailed flatbill (Ramphotrigon ruficauda) is a tyrant flycatcher of lowland Amazonian forests whose basic reproductive biology remains poorly documented. Following hatching, the altricial nestling undergoes a period of rapid feather development and somatic growth in the cup nest. The time from hatching to the achievement of sustained flight and nest departure, known as fledging, occurs at roughly 14 days after hatching [tx = roughly 14 days after hatching] under the warmer thermal regime characteristic of active adult metabolic periods at 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C]. Newly hatched chicks emerge with an initial wet body mass of approximately 2.2 grams [Ww0 = approximately 2.2 grams], a modest starting point consistent with the altricial developmental mode common among tyrant flycatchers.

This represents a nearly nine-fold increase in body mass from the neonatal stage and is achieved through a sustained period of juvenile growth and tissue accumulation. Furthermore, breeding events are infrequent, with individuals producing approximately 2 clutches per year [F_R_i = approximately 2 clutches per year] during the extended rainy season when arthropod prey is most abundant. The first successful breeding attempt, representing the age at which a female completes her initial reproductive bout, has been recorded at approximately 438 days after hatching [tR = approximately 438 days after hatching] when maintained under the standard thermal conditions of 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C].

Metabolic measurements obtained via flow-through respirometry on post-absorptive, resting adults reveal a basal metabolic rate that aligns with the relaxed energetic requirements of a sedentary, lowland insectivore. This value falls within the expected range for a suboscine passerine of this body mass and reflects a metabolic strategy that prioritizes energetic efficiency over high activity rates. Longevity records for this species are not well established from wild banding studies, but maximum lifespan has been estimated at approximately 8.3 years [am = approximately 8.3 years] under the standard active metabolic temperature of 40.2 °C [T = 40.2 °C], a considerable duration for a bird of this size.

The ecological niche occupied by Ramphotrigon ruficauda in the understory of terra firme forests is defined by its dietary specialization on large arthropods and occasional small fruits. The species demonstrates a typical Amazonian life-history syndrome characterized by small clutch sizes and extended parental care periods relative to temperate-zone counterparts.
